code: # 30 provinces over 12 years, one unobserved factor in y and x set.seed(9) d <- expand.grid(year = 1:12, prov = paste0("p", 1:30)) f <- rnorm(12)[d$year] g <- rnorm(30, 1)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))] d$x <- g * f + rnorm(360) d$y <- 1 + 0.7 * d$x + g * f + rnorm(360) r <- ccepnl(d$y, d["x"], d$prov, d$year) r #> ccepnl: common correlated effects, 30 units, 12 periods #> mean group (CCEMG): #>  term       est         se        z            p        lo        hi #>     x 0.7534011 0.06556476 11.49095 1.464985e-30 0.6248965 0.8819056 #> pooled (CCEP): #>  term       est         se        z            p        lo        hi #>     x 0.7581987 0.06456047 11.74401 7.580526e-32 0.6316625 0.8847349 #> heterogeneity bias of CCEP: chi2(1) = 0.0165, p 0.898 r$nfac #>  er thr avg  #>   1   2   2  # a dynamic panel: y depends on its lag; jackknife-corrected mean group set.seed(10) tt <- 40 d <- expand.grid(year = 1:tt, prov = paste0("p", 1:40)) f <- rnorm(tt)[d$year] g <- rnorm(40, 1)[as.integer(substring(d$prov, 2))] d$x <- g * f + rnorm(nrow(d)) d$y <- 0 for (i in which(d$year > 1)) {   d$y[i] <- 0.5 * d$y[i - 1] + 0.7 * d$x[i] + g[i] * f[i] + rnorm(1) } ccepnl(d$y, d["x"], d$prov, d$year, ylag = 1, bias = "jack") #> ccepnl: common correlated effects, 40 units, 40 periods, 1 lags of y, 3 of the averages #> mean group (CCEMG, jack): #>  term       est         se        z            p        lo        hi #>  L1.y 0.5946119 0.04214017 14.11033 3.280167e-45 0.5120187 0.6772051 #>     x 0.6781777 0.06129760 11.06369 1.881911e-28 0.5580366 0.7983187

(2019, JEEM, equation 1, p. 5): county-day # counts on PM2.5 and ozone together, county-by-year-by-month-by-weekday # effects, errors clustered by county (simulated) d$o3 <- rnorm(nrow(d), 0.03, 0.01) ccross(d, "crimes", "area", "day", x = c("pm", "o3"), clus = "area") #> Warning: ccross: fewer than ten clusters; cluster-robust errors are unreliable with so few (wcbx() is made for this case). #> ppmlfe: Poisson pseudo-likelihood, 1460 rows, fixed effects .strat; clustered errors (area; 4) #>  term     est       se    stat         p        lo     hi    rr #>    pm 0.01407 0.002616 5.37971 7.461e-08  0.008946 0.0192 1.014 #>    o3 0.11728 1.936045 0.06058 9.517e-01 -3.677299 3.9119 1.124  # shaped as Han et al. (2026, Methods p. 2 and table 1): city-day # counts, same-weekday-same-month strata, a holiday indicator, natural # splines of temperature (6 df) and humidity (3 df), NO2 at lag 0, the # percent change per interquartile range (simulated) d$no2 <- rnorm(nrow(d), 30, 10) d$temp <- 15 + 10 * sin(2 * pi * as.numeric(d$day) / 365) +   rnorm(nrow(d)) d$rh <- runif(nrow(d), 30, 90) d$hol <- as.numeric(format(d$day, "%m-%d") %in% c("01-01", "10-01")) d$crimes <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(1 + 0.004 * d$no2)) h <- ccross(d, "crimes", "area", "day", x = c("no2", "hol"),             ns = c(temp = 6, rh = 3), clus = "area") #> Warning: ccross: fewer than ten clusters; cluster-robust errors are unreliable with so few (wcbx() is made for this case). b <- h$coef[h$coef$term == "no2", ] 100 * (exp(c(b$est, b$lo, b$hi) * IQR(d$no2)) - 1) #> [1]  1.4930239 -0.7746229  3.8124944 plot(h, terms = "no2")

code: # simulated: an unmeasured shock v multiplies the mean and moves the # exposure; two instruments, day effects, errors clustered by area set.seed(4) d <- expand.grid(day = 1:10, area = 1:40) d$z1 <- rnorm(nrow(d)) d$z2 <- rnorm(nrow(d)) v <- rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.5) d$pm <- 0.6 * d$z1 - 0.4 * d$z2 + v + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.5) d$crimes <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(0.5 + 0.2 * d$pm + v)) f <- expgmm(d, "crimes", endo = "pm", inst = c("z1", "z2"), fe = "day",             clus = "area") f #> expgmm: exponential-mean GMM, multiplicative residual, two-step, 400 rows; errors clustered by area (40) #>  term    est      se  stat       p      lo     hi    rr #>    pm 0.1559 0.06466 2.412 0.01588 0.02921 0.2827 1.169 #> Hansen J = 3.22 on 1 df, p = 0.07274 f$j #>       stat df          p #> 1 3.220049  1 0.07274147 plot(f)  # the additive residual, one step summary(expgmm(d, "crimes", endo = "pm", inst = c("z1", "z2"),                fe = "day", clus = "area", err = "add", step = "one")) #>   term       est         se     stat          p         lo        hi       rr #> 1   pm 0.1582281 0.06382036 2.479273 0.01316505 0.03314248 0.2833137 1.171433

1] + 0.3 * d$enf[i] + u[i] + rnorm(1) } r <- gmmpnl(d$y, d["enf"], d$prov, d$year, gmm = "enf", lagmax = 3,             collapse = TRUE) r #> gmmpnl: system GMM (fd), step 1, 420 rows, 60 groups, 13 instruments #> robust variance #>     term         est         se           z            p         lo        hi #>     L1.y  0.63565326 0.06952086  9.14334550 6.054957e-20  0.4993949 0.7719116 #>      enf  0.92497344 0.19159312  4.82780094 1.380490e-06  0.5494578 1.3004891 #>  (const) -0.06954309 0.13468780 -0.51632809 6.056253e-01 -0.3335263 0.1944401 #>    t2011  0.26161153 0.23231848  1.12609006 2.601274e-01 -0.1937243 0.7169474 #>    t2012 -0.01923081 0.19584762 -0.09819271 9.217793e-01 -0.4030851 0.3646235 #>    t2013 -0.03271092 0.19746408 -0.16565506 8.684284e-01 -0.4197334 0.3543116 #>    t2014  0.19530957 0.21204614  0.92107109 3.570133e-01 -0.2202932 0.6109124 #>    t2015  0.04273779 0.21878075  0.19534529 8.451226e-01 -0.3860646 0.4715402 #>    t2016  0.08698987 0.18530371  0.46944485 6.387517e-01 -0.2761987 0.4501785 #> Wald chi2(8) = 1275.2, p 5.394e-270 #> Wald chi2(8) = 1560.9, p 0 (every coefficient, as xtabond2 prints it) #>                      test       stat df            p #>                     AR(1) -5.0629586 NA 4.127995e-07 #>                     AR(2)  0.6919913 NA 4.889428e-01 #>                    Sargan  8.8777291  4 6.422940e-02 #>                    Hansen  9.3189947  4 5.360236e-02 #>  Hansen without level GMM  0.6621633  2 7.181465e-01 #>      Difference-in-Hansen  8.6568314  2 1.318843e-02 r$tests #>                       test       stat df            p #> 1                    AR(1) -5.0629586 NA 4.127995e-07 #> 2                    AR(2)  0.6919913 NA 4.889428e-01 #> 3                   Sargan  8.8777291  4 6.422940e-02 #> 4                   Hansen  9.3189947  4 5.360236e-02 #> 5 Hansen without level GMM  0.6621633  2 7.181465e-01 #> 6     Difference-in-Hansen  8.6568314  2 1.318843e-02  # the specification of Andreatta et al. 2 * w[, 2] + u + rnorm(nrow(d)) d$out <- 0.5 * d$oz + u + rnorm(nrow(d)) f <- ivfe(d, "out", endo = "oz", inst = colnames(w), fe = c("area", "day"),           se = "twoway") f #> ivfe: two-stage least squares, 720 rows, fixed effects area and day; two-way clustered errors (area, day; 12 and 60) #>  term   est      se  stat        p     lo     hi #>    oz 0.516 0.03059 16.87 3.29e-09 0.4487 0.5833 #> first stage: robust Wald F, Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F, effective F, its keff and 5% critical value (tau 10%): #>  endo  wald    kp   eff  keff    cv ninst #>    oz 489.3 489.3 442.5 1.818 19.73     3 #> over-identification: Sargan, and Hansen J clustered as the first stage: #>    test  stat df       p #>  sargan 5.220  2 0.07353 #>  hansen 3.573  2 0.16752 f$first #>   endo     wald       kp      eff     keff       cv ninst #> 1   oz 489.2895 489.2895 442.5469 1.818342 19.73326     3 f$fstab #>   endo     inst        est        se        rel #> 1   oz  w90_180  2.9213054 0.1237527 10.2179429 #> 2   oz w180_270 -1.9465070 0.1076014 -6.8083594 #> 3   oz   w270_0 -0.0517003 0.1525103 -0.1808338 plot(f)   # shaped as Chen and Li (2020, equations 4-5, p. 4): county-season-year # cells, the triple difference (treated state x summer x after) as the # instrument of the AQI, county-by-year and state-by-season effects # absorbed, the county-by-season effects as indicator columns, errors # clustered by state (simulated) set.seed(14) g <- expand.grid(county = 1:30, season = c("s", "w"), year = 2000:2007) g$state <- (g$county - 1) %/% 3 + 1 g$ddd <- as.numeric(g$state <= 5 & g$season == "s" & g$year >= 2003) g$aqi <- 50 - 6 * g$ddd + rnorm(nrow(g), 0, 3) g$lcrime <- 2 + 0.01 * g$aqi + rnorm(nrow(g), 0, 0.1) g$cy <- paste(g$county, g$year) g$ss <- paste(g$state, g$season) # county x summer, less the first county of each state (the rest is # absorbed by the two sets of effects) for (k in unique(g$county[g$county %% 3 != 1])) {   g[[paste0("cs", k)]] <- as.numeric(g$county == k & g$season == "s") } ivfe(g, "lcrime", endo = "aqi", inst = "ddd",      x = grep("^cs", names(g), value = TRUE), fe = c("cy", "ss"),      clus = "state")$coef[1, ] #>   term        est           se     stat            p         lo        hi #> 1  aqi 0.01381938 0.0009282825 14.88704 1.204632e-07 0.01171945 0.0159193  # shaped as Carrillo, Lopez-Luzuriaga and Malik (2018): the difference # in differences of equation (4), p. 7 (city-day-hour counts, the # treated city after the start, year-month and hour-by-weekday # effects, errors clustered by week) and the spatial regression # discontinuity of equation (6), p. 8 (counts by distance bin, the # inside indicator, a line on each side, within a window) set.seed(15) h <- expand.grid(city = c("quito", "other"), day = 1:120, hour = 0:23) h$after <- as.numeric(h$day > 60) h$treat <- h$after * (h$city == "quito") h$ym <- (h$day - 1) %/% 30 h$hd <- paste(h$hour, h$day %% 7) h$week <- (h$day - 1) %/% 7 h$crimes <- rpois(nrow(h), 2 + 0.3 * h$treat) h$q <- as.numeric(h$city == "quito") ivfe(h, "crimes", x = c("treat", "q"), fe = c("ym", "hd"),      clus = "week")$coef[1, ] #>    term    est         se     stat          p         lo       hi #> 1 treat 0.1875 0.08224276 2.279836 0.03579739 0.01398295 0.361017 b <- data.frame(dist = seq(-975, 975, by = 50)) b$inside <- as.numeric(b$dist > 0) b$dside <- b$dist * b$inside b$n <- rpois(nrow(b), 20 + 5 * b$inside) b$one <- 1 ivfe(b[abs(b$dist) <= 800, ], "n", x = c("inside", "dist", "dside"),      fe = "one", se = "hc1")$coef[1, ] #>     term      est       se    stat          p          lo       hi #> 1 inside 5.968382 3.073507 1.94188 0.05215164 -0.05558163 11.99235

code: # simulated counts; the shock u raises pollution and crime together set.seed(3) d <- expand.grid(day = 1:50, area = 1:15) d$wind <- runif(nrow(d), 0, 360) w <- windiv(d$wind, width = 90) d <- cbind(d, w) u <- rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.5) d$pm <- 2 * w[, 1] - w[, 3] + u + rnorm(nrow(d)) d$crimes <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(1 + 0.1 * d$pm + 0.5 * u)) f <- ppmlcf(d, "crimes", endo = "pm", inst = colnames(w),             fe = c("area", "day"), nboot = 49, seed = 1) f #> ppmlcf: Poisson control function, 750 rows, fixed effects area and day; 49 bootstrap draws of 15 clusters (area) #>     term     est      se  stat         p      lo     hi    rr #>       pm 0.08266 0.03095 2.671 0.0075737 0.02199 0.1433 1.086 #>  vhat:pm 0.14047 0.03845 3.654 0.0002587 0.06512 0.2158 1.151 #> first stage: robust Wald F, Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F, effective F, its keff and 5% critical value (tau 10%): #>  endo  wald    kp   eff  keff    cv ninst #>    pm 255.2 255.2 342.5 2.151 18.98     3 plot(f)  # the paper's plug-in, with its naive errors summary(ppmlcf(d, "crimes", endo = "pm", inst = colnames(w),                fe = c("area", "day"), how = "plug", se = "naive")) #>   term        est         se     stat           p         lo        hi       rr #> 1   pm 0.07803114 0.02424708 3.218167 0.001290126 0.03050775 0.1255545 1.081156

code: set.seed(10) n <- 300 d <- data.frame(prior = rpois(n, 2), age = runif(n, 18, 50),                 t = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)) d$days <- 30 - 6 * d$t + 3 * d$prior - 0.1 * d$age + rnorm(n, sd = 4) rcttml(d, "days", "t", c("prior", "age")) #> rcttml: gaussian outcome, 300 participants; targeted maximum likelihood, g-computation and the difference in means #>  method    est     se     lo     hi         p #>    tmle -6.454 0.4857 -7.406 -5.502 2.775e-40 #>   gcomp -6.454     NA     NA     NA        NA #>   unadj -6.760 0.6640 -8.061 -5.459 2.424e-24 d$rearrest <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 - 0.6 * d$t + 0.4 * d$prior)) rcttml(d, "rearrest", "t", "prior", fam = "binomial")$tab #>   method        est         se         lo          hi           p #> 1   tmle -0.1443982 0.05330437 -0.2488729 -0.03992356 0.006749907 #> 2  gcomp -0.1443982         NA         NA          NA          NA #> 3  unadj -0.1570057 0.05574479 -0.2662635 -0.04774791 0.004854871

code: set.seed(1) n <- 200 df <- data.frame(   a = stats::rnorm(n),   b = stats::rnorm(n),   grade = sample(letters[1:3], n, TRUE) ) df$c <- df$a * 2 + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.1) # strongly related to a df$d <- exp(df$a) # monotone but curved  topcors(df) #> Top correlations (spearman) #>  x y correlation abscor #>  a d      1.0000 1.0000 #>  a c      0.9984 0.9984 #>  c d      0.9984 0.9984 #>  a b     -0.0616 0.0616 #>  b d     -0.0616 0.0616 #>  b c     -0.0597 0.0597  # The curved pair is ranked correctly by Spearman and understated by # Pearson, which is why Spearman is the default. tc <- topcors(df, meth = "spearman") tc[tc$x == "a" & tc$y == "d", "correlation"] #> [1] 1 tp <- topcors(df, meth = "pearson") tp[tp$x == "a" & tp$y == "d", "correlation"] #> [1] 0.8496382  # Filter to the pairs worth looking at, and keep the top two. topcors(df, n = 2, minabs = 0.5) #> Top correlations (spearman) #>  x y correlation abscor #>  a d       1.000  1.000 #>  a c       0.998  0.998  # a threshold above 1 is an error try(topcors(df, minabs = 2)) #> Error : topcors: `minabs` must be a single value in [0, 1].
